current.text: Experts say do not draft him in standard leagues. One calls him an avoid at his ADP in the 120s to 130s. Another does not project him as draftable because the Spurs are so deep.
The latest Spurs projection has him starting next to Fox, Harper, Castle and Wembanyama. The Spurs started three guards in the preseason.
His usage and assists are lower with the current Spurs roster, and he is no longer a high-usage player.
He is expected to lose touches to Dylan Harper and could end up in a low-usage role-player job like Harrison Barnes had.
He is a fixed part of the rotation.
The Spurs are deep, and their players had low minutes last season. Minutes may stay low after the long playoff run.
The roster is very deep at forward. Trades to consolidate it are expected in the fairly near future, but not right now.
For a March 28 season end, the Spurs play 3, 4 and 3 games in our fantasy playoff weeks. They have only 13 back-to-backs.
The Spurs are projected to be one of the top teams in the West. One expert predicts 63 wins.

durable.text: He has had multiple injuries, including several knee problems.
He is an all-around player. He scores, shoots, rebounds, defends and works as a secondary playmaker.

note: He is ranked 162 on Yahoo and 130 on ESPN, priced at about 1 USD on both sites, and went for 5 USD in our league last season. That puts him on the edge of our 144-player draft. His best categories are 2.3 threes and few turnovers, but a 44% FG% hurts, and his role and usage are shrinking behind Harper, Fox and Castle. Do not spend more than 1 USD. Instead, watch him on waivers early in the season, and check whether he keeps a starting spot and about 30 minutes, or ends up in a smaller role-player job.
